title: AES-192: Perfect bit reset: complete key (Blömer–Seifert, FC2003)

target.description: Full AES-192 master key under the perfect bit-reset and observable-correctness model.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Arbitrary key of the stated AES instance in an implementation meeting the fault and feedback assumptions.
setting.plaintext_model: The all-zero128-bit plaintext for initial key addition; longer-key completion uses chosen plaintexts based on the recovered initial128-bit key material.

fault_model.target: State bits immediately after a selected AddRoundKey operation.
fault_model.granularity: One selected state bit per fault-injection attempt.
fault_model.timing: After the initial AddRoundKey and before the first SubBytes; longer-key completion also uses the first encryption round's AddRoundKey.
fault_model.location: The attacker targets the required individual state-bit locations and can move between them.
fault_model.value_control: Force the selected bit to zero; a bit already equal to zero remains unchanged.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Each attempted injection yields a correct/incorrect outcome. Ciphertext-comparison feedback additionally needs a correct reference for the same input, outside the stated attempt count.
fault_model.feedback: Observable correct-versus-incorrect encryption outcome. Section1 permits alternatives: a device reset/error flag; comparison with a fault-free ciphertext; or detectable recomputation timing. Only the binary outcome is required, not the faulty ciphertext bytes.

assumptions: Successful localization and the stipulated fault-value effect are model assumptions, not measured acquisition success rates.
The ciphertext-validity alternatives are interchangeable only as a binary observation; the source does not cost each feedback channel's calibration or reference executions separately.
Recovery target: Full AES-192 master key under the perfect bit-reset and observable-correctness model.
Section4's byte/column and index slips are read with its explicit8lk count and standard four-byte words; the declared target is standard128-bit-block AES.

time.note: No numerical complete-attack offline runtime is reported.

data.note: Direct instantiation of8lk attempts with lk=24 key bytes. For long keys the count includes first128-bit recovery and the remaining64 bits; each target bit requires one ideal reset attempt. Fault-free references are additional if that feedback channel is used.

memory.note: No numerical whole-attack peak-memory budget is supplied.

preprocessing.note: No separate numerical preprocessing time is supplied.

success.description: Deterministic recovery of the stated complete master key in the exact perfect-bit-reset and reliable correctness-feedback model. For a zero state before AddRoundKey, resetting each selected post-addition bit changes the ciphertext iff that key bit is1; the remaining keyed rounds are permutations, so every observed bit decision is exact. The adaptive second stage first recovers the initial128 bits, then zeros the state before round1 AddRoundKey to reveal the remaining64/128 master bits; total192/256 attempts already include both stages. Success1 is an analytical model guarantee, not measured physical fault yield. Selected-bit localization, reset effect and reliable correctness feedback are conditions; any extra correct-reference/calibration cost remains unpriced. The existing standard-AES interpretation of the source byte/word index slips is unchanged.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Theoretical deterministic guarantees require the stated ideal model; local filters, characteristic products, expected counts and physical acquisition are separate. Costs, targets, settings, existing conflicts and full-audit gates are unchanged.

evidence.locator: Section1 p.164; Section4 p.170, both Nk<=Nb and Nk>Nb constructions
evidence.interpretation: Primary-version result with explicit target, feedback model and native fault-attempt accounting; AES means128-bit blocks and the stated standard key size.
Full exact-edition text and AES contribution inventory reviewed; component checks and whole-attack reproduction are separate.

evidence.locator: Proceedings PDF9 / printed170 Section4, perfect-reset bit test and both Nk<=Nb / Nk>Nb constructions; PDF2–3 Sections1/2 for feedback and AES word conventions.
